edges.description: The 5'-regulatory variants are proposed to change IGBP1 expression through altered translational efficiency, mRNA stability, or splicing, shifting Alpha 4 protein dosage.
Because Alpha 4 binds and modulates the PP2A catalytic subunit, altered Alpha 4 dosage is proposed to dysregulate PP2A-dependent dephosphorylation.
Dysregulated PP2A signaling during embryogenesis is proposed to disrupt forebrain commissural development, producing agenesis of the corpus callosum.
Dysregulated PP2A signaling during ocular morphogenesis is proposed to impair closure of the embryonic optic fissure, producing iris and optic nerve coloboma.
Dysregulated PP2A signaling is proposed to disrupt cranial neural-crest and pharyngeal-arch craniofacial and otic morphogenesis, paralleling the craniofacial defects of Opitz GBBB syndrome.
Dysregulated PP2A signaling is proposed to perturb axial and thoracic skeletal morphogenesis and longitudinal somatic growth.
Dysregulated PP2A signaling is proposed to contribute to variable congenital ventricular septal and ductal closure defects, paralleling cardiac midline defects in Opitz GBBB syndrome.

edges.description: Failure of forebrain commissural development directly produces complete absence of the corpus callosum.
Disrupted forebrain commissural and cerebral development contributes to lifelong intellectual disability.
Anterior failure of optic fissure closure leaves a persistent iris cleft.
Posterior failure of optic fissure closure produces coloboma of the optic nerve/disc.
Congenital iris and optic disc coloboma impairs central visual fixation, resulting in secondary congenital nystagmus.
